match.reason: The closest bank card, Writing about experience and the text, covers only linking a question's idea to techniques and effects, not building a whole essay around a clear contention with organised paragraphs, and the other cards cover only parts of the essay (paragraph openings, integrated structure, conclusions, or personal readings), so none teaches the same idea at the right breadth for this VCE Units 3 and 4 text response point.

draft.title: The analytical text response
card: An analytical text response is an essay that answers a topic about a set text. It argues a point of view. It does not retell the story.
the main argument of the whole essay. It answers the topic directly and is stated in the introduction.
each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence that makes one point in support of the contention. The paragraph then backs that point up and links it to the topic.
the essay uses moments, details and short quotations from the text to support each point. The writer then explains how the evidence proves the point.
draft.remember: Answer the topic with a contention, then prove it paragraph by paragraph with explained evidence.

a.q: What is the main job of an analytical text response?
opts: To argue a view that answers the topic
To retell the plot in the order it happens
To list every technique the author uses
To give a personal review of the text
a.why: The essay must argue a contention that answers the topic. Retelling the plot is tempting, but it only reports events and does not argue anything.
a.clue: Think about what the essay must do with the topic.

b.q: Sam is writing about a novel. His paragraph names a scene and describes what happens in it, but says nothing about how it proves his point. What is missing?
opts: Analysis explaining how the evidence supports the point
A longer summary of the scenes before and after it
A second contention for the paragraph to argue
A personal opinion on whether the scene was enjoyable
b.why: Evidence only helps when the writer explains how it proves the point. Sam has described the scene, which is not the same as analysing it. More summary would repeat the same problem.
b.clue: Evidence needs something done with it after it is given.

a.best: To argue a view that answers the topic

b.best: Analysis explaining how the evidence supports the point
